title: Darío
goal: Be told about Rubén Darío by a man who will not stop
culture: Darío was born in Metapa and grew up in León, but when a Nicaraguan says he is de aquí he means the country, and he is right. Every schoolchild here has a poem by heart, which is why the man in the park assumes you will learn one too.

beats.es: Buenas. ¿Y usted sabe quién fue Rubén Darío?
beats.en: Hello. He’s the poet, isn’t he?
ok: buenas el es el poeta verdad
beats.good: El poeta with nothing after it is Darío. There is only one, and everybody knows which one you mean.

beats.es: ¡El poeta! Padre del modernismo. Y es nuestro, ¿oyó? Nuestro.
beats.good: De aquí means Nicaragua, not Granada. Agreeing is the right answer; the geography lesson is not.

beats.es: Repita conmigo, pues: «Margarita, está linda la mar». Apréndaselo.
beats.objective: Tell him you have got it
beats.good: Me lo aprendí, with the me in it, is learning something for yourself. Aprendí on its own sounds like a school report.
De memoria is by heart, and it is the only way anybody here has ever learned a poem. Saying it tells him you did it his way.
